# A DockMaximize continuity red cannot say which exit produced it

## Context

`test/playwright/component/dashboard/DockMaximize.spec.mjs` — the continuity assertion inside *"inside-the-node operations keep maximize, outside operations clear it terminally, and continuity re-applies iff the node survives"* — is intermittent on CI and does not reproduce on a maintainer host. `#18003` owns that defect and stays open for it.

This ticket owns a narrower and separable problem the defect hunt exposed: **when that arm reds, the failure carries no observable that says which of two mechanisms produced it.** Every CI red so far has been an anonymous data point.

The observed failure is always the same on the surface — `expect(locator('.neo-dock-maximized')).toHaveCount(1)` receives `0` for the full 5s poll window, 14 polls, and nothing re-triggers it. Total, not slow.

Live latest-open sweep: checked the latest 20 open issues at 2026-09-01T05:18:29Z; no equivalent found. A2A in-flight claim sweep over the last 30 messages at the same timestamp: no competing `[lane-claim]`/`[lane-intent]` on this scope.

## The Problem

`Neo.dashboard.dock.Workspace#applyDockMaximizePresentation` has **two terminal exits that produce a byte-identical DOM outcome**, and the assertion can only see the DOM:

1. **The fail-safe fired.** `failDockMaximize(nodeId)` sets `maximizedNodeId = null`, because either the tabs node did not resolve (`getDockHost()?.down?.({dockNodeId})` returned nothing) or `measureDockMaximizeRect()` returned `null` — which it does whenever the workspace root measures `0` in either dimension. The transient is gone, so nothing re-applies it. Marker count `0`, permanently.
2. **The write landed and the presentation was lost downstream.** `maximizedNodeId` still holds the id, but the `tabContainer.set({cls, wrapperStyle})` write never reached a live projected node — for instance because a deferred re-projection retired that container instance first. Marker count `0`, permanently.

These are different defects with different owners: (1) is the fail-safe classifying a transient condition as unresolvable; (2) is a lost write. **One config read at failure time separates them**, and the arm currently takes no such read.

The cost is concrete: `#18003` has four CI attempts at one unchanged SHA (3 pass / 1 fail), and the single red cannot be assigned to either family. Any future occurrence is worth the same nothing until the arm reports it.

## The Architectural Reality

- `src/dashboard/dock/Workspace.mjs` — `applyDockMaximizePresentation()` (both fail-guards, then the `tabContainer.set()` write), `failDockMaximize()`, and `measureDockMaximizeRect()` (the `rect?.width > 0 && rect?.height > 0` gate that turns a mid-reflow measurement into a `null`).
- `test/playwright/component/dashboard/DockMaximize.spec.mjs` — the spec already owns a `readWorkspace()` helper over the `Neo.worker.App.getConfigs` RPC, so the observable is one existing call away. No new fixture, no new RPC, no product change.

The assertion itself is correct and stays exactly as it is. Only what a *failure* reports changes.

## The Fix

A `expectMaximizedCount(page, count)` helper in the spec that wraps the existing `toHaveCount` assertion, and on failure appends the `maximizedNodeId` read to the error message before rethrowing. Applied at the continuity assertion — the one that reds, and the only one in the arm following a cross-worker write with no committed operation behind it.

Deliberately **not** a product-side log: that would change runtime behaviour on a path whose timing is the thing under investigation.

## Decision Record impact

`none`.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] **AC-1** The continuity assertion reports `maximizedNodeId`, read at failure time, in the failure message. The assertion's subject, timeout, and expected count are unchanged.
- [ ] **AC-2** Mutation-verified in **both** directions, since one direction alone cannot show the read discriminates:
  - forcing a count mismatch while the node survives reports the surviving id;
  - driving the fail-safe (an unresolvable node id) reports `null`.
- [ ] **AC-3** A read that itself throws (page closed, worker gone) does not replace the real assertion failure — the original error still propagates, carrying a marker instead of the value.
- [ ] **AC-4** The spec passes unchanged otherwise; the arm still pins maximize continuity.

## Out of Scope

- **The `#18003` defect itself.** Determining product-defect vs test-defect, and fixing it, stays there. This ticket makes the next occurrence readable; it does not make it less likely.
- Broadening the helper to every `toHaveCount` in the spec. The other assertions follow committed operations or direct clicks and do not carry the two-exit ambiguity; a blanket swap would be churn.
- Any change to `applyDockMaximizePresentation`, the fail-safe, or the rect gate. If the instrument later shows the fail-safe is misclassifying a transient, that is a product ticket filed on that evidence.

## Avoided Traps

- **Adding a retry or a fixed sleep.** Both would convert an intermittent into a green run — the failure mode `#18001`'s ticket documents in the same subsystem, and Fixed Sleep Lint bans the second outright.
- **Reading the config *before* the wait.** Playwright evaluates an assertion's message argument eagerly, so the obvious one-liner captures pre-wait state and answers the wrong question. The read has to happen in the catch.
- **Treating the local non-repro as settled from one sample per configuration.** The four configurations recorded on `#18003` were one run each — the identical shape whose failure that ticket's AC-1 established. Re-run at 20 samples per configuration before any claim rests on it.
